paper: Witt, J. K. (2019). Graph Construction: An Empirical Investigation on Setting the Range of the Y-Axis. Meta-Psychology, 3, MP.2018.895.
engine: anomalyco/opencode (ReproAI) — DeepSeek V4 Flash via uniGPT
mode: static + independent R & Python reimplementation (not live author-tool execution)
source: Meta-Psychology, 2019, vol 3, MP.2018.895; Open data/materials/reproducible analysis: Yes; Analysis reproduced by Tobias Muhlmeister; DOI 10.5626/MP.2018.895
seed_handling: set.seed(42) in R and a fixed deterministic pipeline in Python. The analysis is closed-form OLS / student-t / analytic BayesFactor (ttest.tstat) — NO simulation/MCMC RNG anywhere, so results are exactly reproducible across runs and languages; seed is informational only.

design.manipulated_factor: y-axis range: full (0-100) vs standardized (mean +/- k SD) vs minimal (data extent +/- 1)
design.measure: per-subject per-condition lm(resp ~ corrCentered): slope=sensitivity, intercept->bias%
design.dz_convention: Lakens (2013) paired dz = |t|/sqrt(n); 95% CI via psych::cohen.d.ci; BF via BayesFactor::ttest.tstat(rscale=0.707 medium prior)

open_artifacts.osf_note: OSF API returned a transient 404 at audit time (2026-09-14) even for the known project; files were retrieved previously and are present locally in data/ and code/.

reimplementation.strategy: Faithful independent reimplementation of the author's per-subject per-condition LM pipeline from raw per-trial data, in BOTH R (exec_check/reimpl_R.R) and Python (exec_check/reimpl_py.py), using the author notebook's documented exclusions and the explicit graphType->condition mapping by NAME.
reimplementation.cross_language_agreement: R and Python agree exactly on every slope M(SD), bias M(SD), t, p, and dz (all closed-form). -> 100% closed-form agreement.
reimplementation.author_script_run: The shipped notebook (Witt_AnalyzeGraphSD_V4.Rmd) hardcodes setwd('C:/Users/jkwitt/Dropbox/InfoVis/bigLittle'); it is an interactive notebook and cannot be run end-to-end as distributed. The analysis is nonetheless fully reproducible from the raw data.
key_results_reproduced: All 5 experiments' all-trial sensitivity slopes M(SD) reproduce to reported 2-dp precision (R==Python).
All 5 experiments' bias % M(SD) reproduce to reported precision.
Every primary paired t-test (t, p, dz) and one-sample bias t-test reproduces within rounding.
Every reported Bayes factor reproduces; every '>100' claim confirmed as a very large BF.
Exp3 main-text subtests reproduce exactly (N=11, df=10).
Exp3 unplanned sub-analyses: all t-values reproduce; reported dz & BF were computed with denominator n=11 (full N) while df is reported as 8 (N=9) - internal inconsistency (ADV-005).
discrepancies: ADV-001: shipped notebook not runnable as distributed (hardcoded path / interactive chunks).
ADV-003: cross-experiment Table A3/A4/A5 Exp1 use exclusion set {1,3}, main text uses {1,8}.
ADV-004: cross-experiment Table A3/A4/A5 Exp3 use the N=9 sub-analysis sample, main text uses N=11.
ADV-005: Exp3 sub-analysis dz & BF use n=11 denominator while df is reported as 8 (N=9).
ADV-006: Exp4 Std-bias test printed t(14) but N=16 -> df=15 (value 0.72 reproduces).
ADV-007: Exp1 incomplete participant '431' vs 430 trials.
ADV-008: Exp4/Exp5 incomplete participants (<480 trials) included without disclosure.
ADV-009: Exp1 Table A5 Full-bias SD reported as 5, computed ~10.2 for any sample; Min-bias SD 21 vs 19.5.
ADV-010: pooled prose percentages (Fig2 '86%' ~86.7%; Fig3 '49%' minimal-big not reproduced - 42-54% by definition).

verdict.headline: The core finding - that a standardized y-axis range of about 1.5 SD improves sensitivity to depicted effect size and reduces bias relative to the full and minimal ranges - is robustly and exactly reproduced from the open data in both R and Python. The primary per-experiment statistics (slopes, bias, t-tests, BFs) reproduce; the caveats are runnability of the shipped notebook and several sample/table-consistency + effect-size-denominator inconsistencies in secondary and summary exhibits.
